paper: Suter et al., Nat Commun 2026, s41467-025-67783-5

findings.title: Pseudoreplication — cells treated as independent biological replicates in limma
findings.snippet: patient_mm <- model.matrix(~0 + patient_group); voom(patient_drugdat, patient_mm); lmFit(patient_y, patient_mm)
findings.reasoning: Each column of patient_drugdat is a CELL not a biological replicate; residual DOF ~N_cells (10^4+) instead of N_patients (11). 15007/18414=81.5% adj.p<.05, 205 P.Value=0 exact, AveExpr 9.806±0.014, B>6500, alisertib t=121.48 logFC=0.083.
findings.suggested_fix: pseudobulk per (patient × condition); OR duplicateCorrelation(block=patientID); OR mixed-effects via muscat/dream

findings.title: `Combination_Index` ≡ |logFC × mRCC| — not a Bliss/Loewe/Chou-Talalay CI
findings.reasoning: Pearson r=1.000000, max abs err 4.99e-08 across all 411 rows. Range 7.2e-08 to 1.23e-03 (3 orders below classical CI scale).
findings.suggested_fix: rename column to scFOCAL_Combination_Score; add Methods sentence clarifying it is custom; fix BLISSS typo at line 813

findings.title: Mean-cutoff dichotomization is circular
findings.reasoning: Labeling cells on the same metric you then test on guarantees ~50/50 split; the limma contrast measures within-population variance. Author's own line-125 comment: 'should the cut-off be set dynamically? i.e. geometric mean of all cells connectivities?'
findings.suggested_fix: external/biology-derived cutoff (e.g., patient-outcome quantile, mixture-model component) or regress against continuous score

findings.title: Headline 'varlitinib' deposited only as `ARRY.334543`, ranks 31/411 not visually-implied top-3
findings.snippet: None — varlitinib appears only as ARRY.334543
findings.reasoning: 0 rows match 'varlitinib' by name; ARRY.334543 at rank 31/411 by CI. Top-3=taselisib(PI3K), volasertib(PLK1), PF.03758309 — none EGFR-targeting, none fits Depatux-M rationale.
findings.suggested_fix: add an alias mapping table to the supp; revise Fig 5c caption to honestly show the rank of each highlighted compound

findings.title: Alisertib doesn't rank near top of own GBM22 PDX contrast (does win every per-patient contrast)
findings.reasoning: PDX axis: alisertib rank 97/1674 by logFC, 166/1674 by |logFC|; top 5 are PMA/ingenol mebutate/paclitaxel — unrelated to aurora kinase. Patient axis: alisertib rank 1/1674 by t in all 11 patients.
findings.suggested_fix: report which design is the actual 'self-validation' in Methods; do not conflate axes

findings.title: ρ=0.7 BLISS validation is aggregate masking per-line heterogeneity
findings.reasoning: Mean per-line ρ=0.317, median 0.255; only 6/24 lines individually p<0.05; 3 with ρ<0 (GSC2 -0.34, GSC38 -0.03, GSC274 -0.03); 18/24 individually NS.
findings.suggested_fix: report per-line ρ distribution; do not headline aggregate; acknowledge framework predicts ~chance per individual line

findings.title: DMSO arm MISSING from Fig 3i deposited data; FDR=3.2e-238 from one-sample-vs-0 test
findings.reasoning: All 41576 rows have Treatment='Alisertib'; zero DMSO rows. DMSO stored as 4 scalar means in Unnamed:31-34. One-sample-vs-0 Wilcoxon on N=10394 yields extreme FDR by N alone; correct two-sample test would weaken by tens of orders of magnitude.
findings.suggested_fix: deposit the per-cell DMSO data (~5708 cells); recompute as two-sample Wilcoxon; report effect sizes prominently alongside FDRs

findings.title: CT-179 GBM8 RNA-seq raw data NOT deposited
findings.reasoning: Paper Fig 4b describes 841-gene CT-179 response signature from R1/R2/R3 per arm; only the derived 411-compound ranking deposited. Combined with F12, the signature derivation is also structurally inflated, but cannot be quantified.
findings.suggested_fix: deposit raw counts and signature derivation script to GEO

findings.title: Fig 5D Vehicle imaging dropout precedes death by 5-7 days (selection bias)
findings.snippet: BLI Vehicle N=[10,10,10,4,3,3,1,1,1,1] for days [0,4,7,11,14,17,20,25,28,32]; first Vehicle death day 17
findings.reasoning: At day 11 all 10 Vehicle mice alive per 5E but BLI N=4. Mice removed from imaging before death (likely humane removal); selectively imaging slower-growing tumors. Vehicle mean trajectory after day 11 biased downward.
findings.suggested_fix: disclose imaging dropout protocol in figure legend; analyze as mixed-effects longitudinal with informative-dropout handling

findings.title: Fig 5D late-timepoint t-tests are degenerate (Vehicle N=1, SD=0)
findings.snippet: Day 25: Vehicle Mean=2.38e9 SD=0 N=1; Combo Mean=9.16e6 SD=7.98e6 N=10; t=297.142, 'p<0.000001'
findings.reasoning: Standard two-sample t undefined at N=1; effectively one-sample test using only Combo's variance. Rerun restricted to days with N≥3 both arms: max valid t=3.13 at day 17, p~0.005-0.01.
findings.suggested_fix: restrict per-timepoint comparisons to days with N≥3 in all arms; use mixed-effects longitudinal model; rely on Fig 5E survival as primary evidence

findings.title: Excel SEPT/MARCH gene-symbol corruption in supp_dataset1 + supp_dataset3
findings.reasoning: 15 distinct symbols in ds1, 20 in ds3. ds2 has properly-coded MARCH1-9 + SEPT2-11 — proves ds1+ds3 went through Excel but ds2 didn't (two export paths or post-hoc editing). Each '1-Mar' ambiguously collapses MARCH1 ∪ MARC1 ∪ MARCHF1. Strong provenance marker.
findings.suggested_fix: re-export from FindAllMarkers objects with options(stringsAsFactors=FALSE); never round-trip through Excel; remap via HGNC date→symbol crosswalk

findings.title: CellClusteringOnConnectivity_V5.R only processes one patient (GBM41)
findings.reasoning: Active line 63 overrides commented-out line 62. Part 2 reads _metadata_with_clusters.rds files via list.files() — silent disk aggregation. Deposited s3b covers 13 patients × 7 k-means, so actual analysis iterated more than committed code does.
findings.suggested_fix: uncomment line 62; delete line 63; replace silent file aggregation with in-memory result aggregation; add fail-loud if expected patients missing

findings.title: 200nM.R: positional replicate + adj.p/raw-p switch + circular LFC cutoff
findings.snippet: pheno$replicate <- c('1','2','3','1','2','3'); ...; sigres2 <- subset(resLFC_DF, resLFC_DF$pval < .05 & abs(log2FoldChange) > logFC_t)
findings.reasoning: Line 84 volcano uses padj<0.05; line 130 silently switches to raw p (likely typo since DESeq2 column is 'pvalue' not 'pval' — may yield NA). Either way the gene-list driving singscore + connectivity is on a different basis than the figure-colored one. Line 79 logFC_t computed from same fit then re-used.
findings.suggested_fix: construct pheno from sample names with stringr regex + stopifnot; use consistent (padj or pvalue) across volcano and gene-set extraction; pre-register LFC threshold or report across a range

findings.title: '54 of 64' drug count unreproducible — deposit has 51 drugs
findings.reasoning: Header has 51 drug-name columns; no contrast in deposited limma block reaches 54 sig. Methods says 63, Results says 64. Either Methods/Results inconsistency or deposit is a 51-of-64 subset.
findings.suggested_fix: reconcile Methods/Results drug count; deposit the full drug set; clarify which subset is plotted in Fig 2h

findings.title: Two unrelated tables glued vertically under shared column names (Fig 2h + s9b/c)
findings.snippet: Fig 2h block 1: 4×51 connectivity scores. Block 2: limma topTable with row-6 sub-header remapping drug column names to {logFC, AveExpr, t, P.Value, adj.P.Val, B, contrast, compound}
findings.reasoning: Naïve pd.read_csv mixes blocks; 'alisertib' column carries t=55.30 instead of scaled connectivity 0.0046. s9b/c has 3 blocks.
findings.suggested_fix: split into separate CSVs per block; or sentinel-pad with a blank header row + explicit second header

findings.title: 5 L1000 compounds silently dropped from limma roster (1679 → 1674)
findings.reasoning: 5/1679 = 0.3% drop; undocumented; cannot tell if technical or signal-based
findings.suggested_fix: add a QC manifest documenting compounds dropped and why

findings.title: 978 vs 961 landmark genes
findings.reasoning: 17-gene shortfall (1.7%); connectivity scores not bit-reproducible
findings.suggested_fix: reconcile count; deposit the exact landmark set used (with version/release ID)

findings.title: CT-179 monotherapy NOT significant vs vehicle (HR≈1, p=0.611)
findings.snippet: Vehicle MS=19d, CT-179 MS=24d, p=0.611 NS; ABT-414 alone MS=38d p=0.0006; Combo MS=63d vs ABT-414 alone p=0.0014
findings.reasoning: Combo > ABT-414 alone IS supported, but 'OLIG2 inhibitor as therapy' implies monotherapy efficacy that data doesn't support. Discussion overstates.
findings.suggested_fix: explicitly acknowledge CT-179 monotherapy NS in abstract/discussion; frame as 'sensitization to ABT-414' rather than 'OLIG2 inhibitor therapy'

findings.title: OPC story untestable for GBM47, GBM53 (OPC proportion ~0.0005)
findings.reasoning: True biological scarcity, not data gap. Paper doesn't acknowledge hypothesis is unmeasurable in 2/11 patients.
findings.suggested_fix: note in OPC discussion that hypothesis is tested in 9/11 patients

findings.title: Fig 3i `Subtype` is long-form key (4 rows/cell) — quadruple-count hazard
findings.reasoning: 41576 = 10394 × 4 subtypes; re-user joining to per-cell metadata without dedup will 4×-count
findings.suggested_fix: document grain in supp legend; OR re-deposit as wide-form (one row per cell with 4 score columns)

findings.title: ds5p ↔ ds5pdx are different experiments — not a parent/child FK
findings.snippet: patient: 18414 rows = 11 contrasts × 1674 compounds; pdx: 1674 rows = 1 contrast × 1674
findings.reasoning: 100% compound overlap (NOT 9.1% as enrichment said); different experiment contrasts (within-patient vs PDX drug-vs-DMSO); not row-level FK
findings.suggested_fix: none — enrichment description; consider noting in deposit that the two files share vocabulary not rows

findings.title: panobinostat_inverseCor sign-flip risk
findings.reasoning: Pipeline holds both; UMAP plots _inverseCor while cell-typing uses raw; figure↔table sign-flip risk
findings.suggested_fix: pick one convention; delete the other column; document with a single Methods sentence

findings.title: 75th-percentile per-sample feature cutoff drops healthiest cells
findings.snippet: cutoff <- quantile(obj.list[[i]]$nFeature_RNA)[4]; subset(... nFeature_RNA > 200 & nFeature_RNA < cutoff)
findings.reasoning: By construction drops top 25% of features per sample (often healthiest); affects all downstream cell-state composition
findings.suggested_fix: use DoubletFinder/scDblFinder; OR median + 3*MAD; OR 95-99th percentile

findings.title: bliss_scores strsplit(..., '...', fixed=T) fragile to dot-containing LINCS names
findings.reasoning: LINCS compounds with dots (PF.03758309, NVP.TAE684, GSK.1070916, ARRY.334543) silently truncate Drug2 if adjacent; no current failure but latent
findings.suggested_fix: use non-dot delimiter; OR exact-match join against compound vocab

findings.title: library(lme4) loaded but never used — fossil of the correct fix for F1
findings.snippet: library(lme4) # never invoked anywhere in scFOCAL-dataProcessing
findings.reasoning: Unused lme4 is exactly the tool needed to fix F1's pseudoreplication; suggests authors knew about mixed-effects fix and didn't apply

findings.title: pct.1=0 absence-markers (mitochondrial/housekeeping picked as 'markers')
